In detail

No current dated crime-specific press coverage was found for this quartier. An older (2014) opinion piece described disorder around rue de Lappe/rue de la Roquette, but it's too dated to reflect today's situation, and a 2025 report on rue de Lappe actually describes the bar scene there declining (post-Covid, post-Olympics) rather than any safety-driven exodus. This is Paris's well-known Bastille nightlife pocket, so normal weekend-crowd/pickpocket awareness applies, but nothing documented rises above that. Sources checked: Sortiraparis, on rue de Lappe's declining bar scene, Aug 2025.

Hidden gem · Paris

Craftsmen

Microbrewery136 boulevard Voltaire, 75011Tue–Thu 17:00–00:00 · Fri–Sat 17:00–01:00

The 11th sends most visitors to rue de Lappe and Oberkampf. This is the same arrondissement, eight minutes' walk, and nobody is queueing.

Beer brewed on the premises by Thibault and Florian, poured a few hundred metres from the Bastille crowds and a world away from them in volume. Sharing boards to go with it, wine and alcohol-free options if beer is not your thing, and room for twenty to forty if you are taking over a corner. Opens at five, closes at one on Fridays and Saturdays.
